newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WESTNER GIVES SOUTH AFRICA PLACE IN DUNHILL CUP SEMIS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WESTNER GIVES SOUTH AFRICA PLACE IN DUNHILL CUP SEMIS.

text.p: Wayne Westner made a magnificent birdie three at the tough 17th hole to win the deciding match on Saturday as third-seeded South Africa reached the Dunhill Cup semifinals with a 2-1 win over Ireland.

After Ernie Els had lost his match against Paul McGinley, Westner rifled a 195-yard five-iron at the dangerous "Road Hole" on the Old Course that finished just 3-1/2 feet from the flag. He then sank the birdie putt to take a one-stroke lead over Padraig Harrington.

Par at the last hole left him a 69-70 winner and put South Africa through after Retief Goosen, forsaking his driver to hit irons off the tees, had beaten Darren Clarke on the first playoff hole with a 20-foot birdie putt.
Els lost 69-71 to McGinley.
The top-seeded United States beat Spain 3-0 to clinch their place in Sunday morning's semifinals. The final will be held in the afternoon.

For the Americans Mark O'Meara recovered his form after a losing 75 on Friday to beat Miguel Jimenez 67-68 with a birdie at the last, Steve Stricker birdied four of the last six holes to beat Diego Boreggo 70-74 and Phil Mickelson played superbly to crush Ignacio Garrido 66-77.
Both those semifinalists had to wait until later in the day to know their opponents
After Harrington birdied the 15th to go one ahead, Westner replied with an 18 foot birdie at the 16th to level the match again.
His drive at the 17th was not perfect. "For the second shot I wanted to be up on the top level to give myself a birdie chance.
"I saw the shot I wanted to hit and hit it just like I saw it. It hit at a 180 yards and took a nice bounce up close."
After losing his first two matches with scores of 76 and 78, Goosen decided to abandon his driver on Saturday and hit irons off the tee.
"I decided to hit shots that I know I can hit. Darren was 50 yards passed me on most holes but I was hitting my approach shots first and getting them in there. That kept the pressure on him."
Clark, who holed from 15 feet at the 18th for a birdie to force the playoff, missed from 20 feet before Goosen rolled in his putt from the same distance for the victory.
Els was pleased to be pulled through by his team mates, but Clark was disconsolate. "It's the most disappointed I have ever felt," he said.
"I think we had the team to win this tournament. I don't think they outplayed us today, they just had all the luck."
O'Meara, who played in the first three Dunhill Cups from 1985 to 1987 without ever being on a winning team, was pleased to have another chance.
He was also pleased to get his swing back after suffering in the wind on Friday.
Stricker's best birdie came at the 17th where he holed from 40 feet.
Mickelson, leader of the U.S. money list, is thoroughly enjoying being at the old home of golf at St Andrews.
"It's not so much what I've learned about the course. It's what I've experienced walking the fairways that Bobby Jones walked 100 years after the game began," he said.
"Seeing the old town and the university, I'm just enjoying being here."
The dream of 1,000-1 outsiders India came to an end when they were beaten 3-0 by Sweden, who go through to meet the United States in their semifinal.
